rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.err.c3b3.2: The black king goes to d6 and watches the three key squares; from b3, your king cannot take the opposition.

rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.err.d3d4.2: With the pawn on d4, the key squares move up to c6, d6 and e6, and the black king takes d6.

rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l1: Notice: the kings are on the same diagonal, the slanted line c4, d5, e6, with just one square between them, d5.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l2: This is called diagonal opposition. As with direct opposition, the side not to move has it: here, White.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l3: Black takes the king to d6 and watches c5, d5 and e5.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l4: You face it from d4: the diagonal opposition becomes direct opposition, and it is still yours.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l5: The black king must give way: wherever it goes, your king gets into a key square.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l6: The black king gives way to c6, trying to watch c5 and d5.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l7: Your king gets into e5, a key square. The pawn will promote.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l8: Now imagine that, instead of taking the king to d4, White pushes the pawn.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l9: As in the first chapter, the pawn moved too early: the black king faces yours from c6, and the opposition is Black's.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l9b: It is a draw: the king goes first, and the pawn afterwards.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l10: Let's go back to the first move. What if the black king goes to e5, close to the pawn?
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l11: The black king goes to e5, and your king gets into c5, a key square: once there, White wins.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l12: What if, with the black king on e5, White pushes the pawn?
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l12b: It does not work: the black king comes back in front of the pawn, to d6, and it is a draw.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l13: Let's go back to the position after the first move.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l14: Kings on the same diagonal, with one square between them: the opposition belongs to the side not to move, and one move makes it direct.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l15: Now let's see the defence: Black can use the diagonal opposition too.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.e1: Now you play Black, and the board turns around.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.e2: The white king wants to reach d4, e4 or f4, the pawn's key squares.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.e3: Your king must close that path, and the means is the same as in attack: taking the opposition.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.certo: Exactly! Now the diagonal opposition is yours.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.revela: The best is to take the king to e5, on a diagonal with the white king: the opposition passes to Black.

rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.err.e6d7.2: The white king gets into f4, a key square, before your king can watch it. The pawn will promote.

rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.err.e6f7.2: The white king gets into f4, a key square, before your king can watch it. The pawn will promote.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.err.e6d6.1: With this move your king stays off the white king's diagonal, and White finds the way.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.err.e6d6.2: The white king gets into f4, a key square: from d6, your king cannot take the opposition.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.err.e6d5.1: Going to d5, toward the pawn, your king leaves f4 unwatched.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.err.e6d5.2: The white king gets into f4, the key square your king left free, and the pawn will promote.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.err.e6f6.1: With this move your king stays off the diagonal, and White takes the opposition.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.err.e6f6.2: The white king goes to f4, a key square, facing yours: the direct opposition belongs to White.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.err.e6f5.1: Going straight to f5, your king lets White take the opposition.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.err.e6f5.2: The white king goes to f3 and faces yours: the direct opposition belongs to White.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.livre.fala: Keep playing with Black and see how White attacks.

rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.fins.limite: The white king controls the key squares: the pawn will promote.

rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.fins.capturado: The pawn fell: your king won the fight for the key squares, and it is a draw.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.fins.afogado: The black king has no move and is not attacked: it is a draw, and the defence held.

rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.l1: The kings are on the same diagonal, with one square between them, f4, and White is to move: the opposition is yours.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.l2: The white king goes to f3, next to the key squares.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.l3: You face it from f5: the diagonal opposition becomes direct, and it is still yours.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.l4: The white king must give way, and your king keeps watching the key squares. It is a draw.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.l5: Let's go back to the white king on f3. What if your king goes to d4, toward the pawn?
